memories.content: Link each HCI research question directly to corresponding user data and analysis procedures.
In preregistered studies, specify the conditions under which deviations from the plan are permissible.
In preregistered studies, specify how to record content that deviates from the plan.
Commit to one exact target number of participants so the schedule, workload, and budget can be checked against the same quantity.
Specify the interview protocols, recording devices, or log tools used to collect each type of user data.
Specify whether each type of user data is collected before, during, or after the interaction.
Readers cannot tell whether the schedule and budget agree when different sections imply different target counts.
In formative evaluation prototypes, implementation instability exists as an independent cause of task failure alongside design choices.
If a prototype safety signal occurs during formative evaluation, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over planned data collection.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to the data and analysis.
The author of this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Calculate the required sessions, facilitator hours, and participant payments from the same exact target rather than from separate rough estimates.
If recruitment falls below the exact target, state the shortfall explicitly and revise the affected schedule or deliverable.
Do not use a wide range merely to postpone choosing the quantity that the rest of the proposal must support.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames overlap only in compensation-budget construction, where exact participant volume and per-participant burden are complementary inputs. The reference otherwise emphasizes methodological traceability, preregistration, data collection, participant-count consistency, prototype risks, and proposal framing; the compared frame adds detailed compensation and payment policies.

relations.reason: The reference requires payments and related resources to derive from one exact target, while the compared frame bases compensation budgets on session, technical-preparation, and travel burden. These complementary inputs jointly support the same budgeting decision.
relations.summary: Participant-payment budgeting uses explicit operational drivers: a consistent participant target and the estimated burden borne by each participant.

relations.reason: The reference states both the traceability requirement and its role in reviewer judgments; the compared frame contains no corresponding methodological claim.
relations.summary: Research questions should be directly traceable to the user data and analysis procedures that make them answerable.

reports.both: Both frames require participant-payment budgets to be grounded in explicit planning inputs: participant volume and participation burden.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely addresses burden-sensitive and actual-time compensation, payment-method flexibility, withdrawal payments, and separating participant compensation from staff labor.
reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely covers research-question traceability, preregistration deviations, collection methods and timing, exact recruitment targets, prototype instability and safety, and proposal framing.
